title: Replication code and Supplementary Material: Pricing geopolitical risk into delivered green hydrogen costs (Algeria-EU, 2026 Strait of Hormuz closure)
description: Route-explicit deterministic delivered-cost model for green hydrogen supplied to the EU from Algeria (pipeline and ammonia) and five competitors (Morocco, Egypt, Oman, Australia, Chile), with country WACC and default-spread betas, bottom-up shipping, canal tolls and war-risk insurance with rerouting; Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 draws), Shapley decomposition, ES95 security premium, break-even GPR, Sobol indices, and an ex-post scenario tested on the observed 2026 Strait of Hormuz closure. All inputs are documented with their sources in params/; outputs are regenerated by src/run_model.py. Version 2.1.0 accompanies the revised article: the PV electricity cost uses the yield after clipping, the reference voyage of the ammonia chain is valued at the baseline production cost, three bounding variants are added (midstream financing, fuel valuation, independent PV yield factors) and further dated 2026 war-risk quotes are included (see CHANGELOG.md). It supersedes v2.0.0 and v1.0.0.
